Groups reuse outbound proxy paths, not entire profile configurations. Only the special Live Routing connection uses these groups and rules with global connection settings. Regular profile connections use their own configuration with global settings and Core Routing; they ignore the saved Live Routing plan.

In a Live Routing session, rules run top to bottom; the first matching enabled rule wins, ahead of Core Routing. Apps and domains must both match when both are set; values within either list match any. After those rules, unmatched traffic follows the default route. Applied changes affect new connections only; existing connections keep their paths.
Apps Routing still controls which apps enter the VPN. Excluded apps never reach these rules. Domain matches need a domain known to Xray (DNS or sniffing); an IP-only connection may not match.

The first eligible node wins: primary, then numbered backups. Choose the primary with a radio button or use arrows to change priorities. A recovered higher-priority node is used again for new connections only. OK keeps the draft; Save applies it.

Select members across subscriptions. With Select, the radio button sets the preferred primary, not necessarily the node currently used. Edit numbered backups in Primary and backup order. Random and Round robin use all eligible members, without priorities. OK keeps the draft; Save applies it.
Availability filters participants only. All healthy members participate; list order is not a primary/backup priority.
Group edits are not applied. Confirm selections, then Save. Runtime node labels are hidden until the group matches.
Availability checks are off. No health-based filtering or automatic failover.

Profiles are matched within their subscription by name and configuration, never by list position. Reordering alone keeps group membership. A rename with unchanged configuration and a configuration edit with a unique unchanged name retain identity. JSON formatting does not change identity. Exact duplicate occurrences are paired deterministically.

Deleted profiles and ambiguous changes receive no automatic replacement. Changed configurations with duplicate names, or simultaneous name and configuration replacements, can leave old group members missing. Review content changes and missing members after a refresh.

Refresh can immediately update an active Live Routing session. If inspection must happen before use, stop Live Routing, refresh, review the groups and reconnect. A missing member rejects Live Routing start or update; the running session can retain its last-applied configuration while the database is newer. Check Connect for errors rather than assuming a local save was applied. Regular profile connections ignore the saved plan and remain usable without editing or deleting it.

1. Import the profiles you need.
2. Add a named group and choose its members, including members from different subscriptions if needed.
3. Choose Select, Random, Round robin or Least ping. Availability checks are optional for the first three and always enabled for Least ping. For health-enabled Select, arrange the primary and backups; Least ping uses priority to break equal-delay ties.
4. Choose the default group. Add app/domain rules, choose their targets and arrange rules from specific to general.
5. Set the shared availability interval under Settings → Preferences → Basic → Live Routing if needed, then save.
6. Save the routing plan. In Connect, select the special Live Routing group and connect without choosing a profile. Only this connection uses the plan; regular profile connections ignore it. Check Connect for runtime errors; unsaved edits are not active.

A Live Routing connection requires at least one group. Its default group carries unmatched proxy traffic and Core Routing proxy targets. Until you choose a default explicitly, the first group is used. Core Routing direct and block rules still handle traffic not already matched by a live rule.

A matching live rule targeting Default route chooses the default group immediately; later Core Routing rules are not evaluated for that flow. Unmatched traffic continues through Core Routing and the default group. Regular profile connections instead use the selected profile with global settings and Core Routing. They do not read or apply any Live Routing groups or rules.

Groups reuse outbound paths, including their dependencies, not the whole member configuration. Member inbounds, DNS and unrelated routing settings do not replace the global settings of the Live Routing connection.

Select without availability checks uses the configured member without testing or automatic failover. With checks enabled, it chooses the first eligible member in the explicit primary/backup order. A recovered higher-priority member is preferred again after the recovery threshold.

Random and Round robin distribute each new connection among all eligible members when checks are enabled. Availability is a filter, not a priority system; there is no single active member.

Least ping always checks availability and chooses the eligible member with the lowest last successful measured HTTP delay. Configured priority breaks ties. One transient failure retains the last successful delay until failure thresholds remove the member. New measurements affect new connections; established connections keep their paths.

App only: choose a browser, leave domains empty and target a browsing group. Its traffic reaching the VPN matches regardless of domain.

Domain only: leave apps empty and enter example.com to match that domain and its subdomains. Use full:example.com for that exact name only.

App AND domain: choose a video app and enter domain:example.com. The rule matches only connections from that app to that domain or its subdomains. Other domains from the same app continue to later rules.

Order matters: put a specific app-and-domain block rule above a broader app-to-group rule. Otherwise the broader rule wins first. Multiple apps within the app list are alternatives, as are multiple domains within the domain list.

Failover: configure A as primary, B as backup 1 and C as backup 2 with checks enabled. If A becomes unavailable, new connections use B if eligible, otherwise C. If all are unknown or down, the group blocks new traffic; it never escapes through a different default group.

Checks start immediately and perform HTTP GET to the Ping Address in Settings through each exact member outbound path. Only HTTP 2xx succeeds; redirects are not followed. Manual ping type and timeout do not change these checks.

Settings → Preferences → Basic → Live Routing controls the shared interval: 5–3600 seconds, 10 by default. Saving it updates only an active health-enabled Live Routing session without reconnecting. Each probe times out after 5 seconds, with at most four probes across all groups; large groups can queue. User connections do not trigger extra probes.

An untested member is ineligible until its first success. Two consecutive failures remove a member; three consecutive successes restore it. Observations expire after three intervals plus 5 seconds and then need three successes again. At the default interval, unqueued failure detection is roughly 10–25 seconds and recovery 20–35 seconds. Longer intervals slow both. These are not user-connection timeouts.

Unknown is not healthy. Without an eligible member, including startup and controller errors, new group traffic is blocked without direct or default-route fallback.

A successful HTTP check proves only that this HTTP test worked through that outbound at that moment. It is not a full TCP/UDP test and does not guarantee every website, DNS request, app or protocol. A failing test endpoint can make otherwise usable nodes unavailable. Checks consume traffic and battery.\n\nHealth changes and saved routing updates affect new decisions. Established connections are not migrated, replayed or retried. For Select, Random and Round robin, turning checks off restores unchecked behavior, not guaranteed availability. Least ping requires checks; choose another strategy to disable them.
Draft, saved plan and running plan

A picker changes the draft only after OK. Save stores the plan locally and asks only an active Live Routing session to apply it. Regular profile sessions are unaffected. Saving does not start a stopped session, reconnect, change connection mode or prove that the core accepted the update. Open Connect if an update fails.\n\nStatus is matched against the strategy, preferred member, ordered membership and the configuration fingerprint of every member. If the draft is unsaved, the runtime differs, a profile changed after refresh or status cannot be read, the editor will not label a current database entry as active. A group may also be loaded without any rule currently sending traffic to it. Healthy and eligible do not mean that an established connection is using that member.
App identity is not an app name

App matching requires Android 10 or newer, VPN mode with owner identification and authenticated local SOCKS. In SOCKS-only mode, use domain rules. Live Routing is unavailable in transparent root mode and this screen cannot save in that mode.

Managed UID accounts share the local SOCKS password. A direct SOCKS client holding that password can claim a managed app identity: routing is not an authorization boundary against that client. Do not share the credentials with untrusted clients.

Live Routing does not disable inbound authentication, Apps Routing or owner-protection policy. Real TUN flows pass admission checks before receiving a SOCKS identity. Traffic rejected or excluded by those mechanisms cannot be recovered by adding a Live Routing rule. Unknown owners do not satisfy app criteria. Clear app criteria from enabled rules before saving in a mode that cannot match apps.

Off: app split routing is disabled. All user app traffic goes through the VPN.

Exclude selected apps: the apps you choose bypass the VPN, and all other apps continue using the VPN.

Include only selected apps: only the apps you choose use the VPN, and all other apps bypass it.

Use Off when you want one simple full-device tunnel. Use Exclude when most apps should stay inside the tunnel and only a few should bypass it. Use Include when the VPN is needed only for a small set of apps.

The curved arrows undo and redo edits. The magnifier opens find and replace; Match case is available in the options menu while search is open.

The <> button formats JSON without changing its values. Syntax is checked automatically: tap the red status at the bottom to move to the reported error.

The symbol row inserts punctuation and indents or outdents text. The three-dot menu controls font size and line wrapping.

Profile details (the sliders button) contains the name and group. The top checkmark saves the profile and checks the generated configuration with Xray. Valid JSON alone does not guarantee a valid Xray configuration.
